concerns.message: The hold grace of 30 frames (500 ms) is counted from the last message received, but a held key is only resent every 100 ms (`inputSender.ts` REFRESH_MS, and the headless `hold()` loop uses `sleep(100)`, which drifts). A transport stall of S ms therefore produces a gap between received messages of S to S+100 ms if the held messages are flushed when the stall ends, or S to S+200 ms if they are dropped. For the acceptance's 300–450 ms stalls, the upper end reaches 550–650 ms, over the 30-frame window. `InputGate` lapses at `frame - heldAtFrame > N`, the check runs only on world ticks (every 3 frames), and the shared machine adds timer drift. The browser test's 400 ms pause sits at 400–500 ms, which is on the edge.
concerns.consequence: The item-0 integration test with a 450 ms stall fails about half the time, depending on when the stall starts relative to the resend, and the browser hold test flakes. The worker then either weakens the test or changes a constant the acceptance fixes, and real gaps near 500 ms still cancel holds, so the operator's playtest bug stays partly unfixed. Settle this before starting: either make WORLD_HOLD_GRACE_FRAMES cover the stall plus one resend period (for example 36 frames, 600 ms; a 700 ms stall still cancels), or cap the tests at 400 ms with flush semantics. The rule should state gaps as time between received messages.

concerns.message: Tonic purchases and rumor purchases share the ledger's per-player request-id space. `chargeRumor` (apps/server/src/intel.ts:286) passes the client's raw rumor id to `purchase` and throws on any refusal or replay. The room checks for repeats only in its own rumor record (`this.rumors.decided`), which knows nothing of tonic ids. A client that buys a tonic with id "x" (or has one refused and kept) and then sends a rumor request with id "x" gets past every room check. `purchase` then returns `duplicate` because the item differs, `chargeRumor` throws inside `stepReveals`, the world tick's catch calls `fault`, and the match is aborted with no winner. The plan says only that purchases "use per-player request ids" and that the shop's rumor purchase is "the same flow as the journal's"; it does not say how the two id streams are kept apart.
concerns.consequence: A modified client, or a bug in the shop's id counter, can abort any match it is in (§12 fault path), which §16 forbids for duplicate requests. Room-level refusals that the ledger never keeps (`not-at-dock`, `not-in-play`, `busy`) also have no stated replay rule for tonics. Before starting, decide either to prefix ledger request ids by item (`rumor:`/`tonic:`) or to have the room refuse cross-item reuse as `duplicate` before charging, and add an integration test that reuses one id across the tonic and rumor messages.

concerns.message: Acceptance 3 asks for the tonic to give 110/100 speed "in both the simulation and the prediction replay (the hash matches)", and the constraint says this is "so client prediction and the server agree". The sea has no client prediction: docs/architecture.md says "The sea does not predict; the duel arena does", and the web client never calls `step`/`sail`. The tonic is also started by the room through the ledger (`useTonic`), not by an input `step` sees, so replaying an input log alone does not reproduce it.
concerns.consequence: A worker may start building sea prediction, which blows the three-hour deadline, or write a replay test that never exercises the tonic. The intended test is presumably a deterministic replay of `step` plus the room's activation events, with `hashState` covering the new ShipState field; say so.

concerns.message: If the grace is put inside `InputGate.inputAt`/`lapsedAt`, it also changes what `step()` receives. Today a lapsed gate gives no entry, so a moored ship keeps its `mooredThrottle`. With the grace in that path, it receives `{moveY:0, E}`, which resets `mooredThrottle` to 0. A player moored while holding W+E is then cast off when they later release E, which breaks the documented rule that keys still held after a stall do not cast off. The same applies to the treasure-claim and fruit paths.
concerns.consequence: This could regress the sail-and-dock, theft-loop or full-match scenarios, or cause a subtle mooring bug after network gaps. Put the grace in a separate accessor (for example `worldHoldButtonsAt(frame)`) that only `stepChannels`, `stepFruits` and `stepClaim` read, and leave the simulation's input path unchanged.

concerns.message: Acceptance 0 expects the collect cancelled by a 700 ms stall to report reason `released`. That reason exists only in the treasure-claim module (`ClaimInterruptReason`). The ledger's `cancelChannel` for collects and cache claims has no reason, and the room's notices record only collected, claimed or failed.
concerns.consequence: The worker has to add a room-level cancel-reason notice and a protocol field for collects. Otherwise the test asserts something that is never sent, or checks only that progress reset.

concerns.message: If T is a button bit in the input stream (latched and resent every 100 ms while held), the room calls `useTonic` on every world tick while T is held. That produces `tonic-active` refusals on every tick, and every ledger rejection is pushed to `this.refusals`. A T held or latched just after a tonic expires drinks the second tonic unintentionally. There is also a one-tick mismatch to settle: the ledger's effect covers ticks t to t+239, while the simulation step for tick t has already run when the room processes the activation.
concerns.consequence: Players could lose tonics unintentionally, the refusal log would fill with noise, and the ledger's `activeTonic` and HUD timer would disagree by one tick with the boosted movement, making the "exactly 240 ticks" test ambiguous. Make drinking edge-triggered (a message with a request id, or a rising edge), and state which ticks are boosted.

concerns.message: Carried item 8c asks the raw-frame privacy test to scan for the sources' and caches' exact coordinates. Sources and caches both sit at dock centres (`sourceSites`/`dockCentre`), and a moored ship is snapped to exactly that point. In the existing test the thief and the stranger moor at docks, so their own ship state legitimately carries those coordinates. The coordinates are also binary-encoded numbers in Colyseus frames, so a byte search for small integers is prone to coincidental matches.
concerns.consequence: As written, the scan either fails on legitimate own-ship positions or is quietly made hollow (for example, searching for JSON text that never appears in binary frames). Define it as: scan only for coordinates the client could not know (sources and caches on islands it never moored at, ships not in sight), using the schema's number encoding.

concerns.message: The browser check "covers more distance over two seconds than without the tonic" compares a 10% difference. Wall-clock sampling of interpolated positions (patches at 20 Hz, drawn 100 ms behind), acceleration to the new maximum, and load on the shared machine each add several percent of noise. Both runs also need open water for the full 2 s without running aground.
concerns.consequence: The shop-and-tonic scenario could flake in the verifier. Measure over server world ticks (patched `worldTick` deltas) or compare the integer speed readout at steady state, not wall time.

concerns.message: Several items add real-time work to a 3-hour lane with 18 s of integration headroom (192 s now, 210 s allowed). The branch table requires deleting each branch and running tests in parallel batches on a shared machine. The new hold tests are timing-sensitive, with real-time 300–700 ms stalls and 6 s collects. The crate same-tick tie also has to be forced: `MatchState.ships` is in join order, not id order, so the room must sort before calling `grantGold` (whose reason is `supply-cache`, not `supply`), and placing both ships needs the pause and step hooks.
concerns.consequence: Parallel mutation runs can make timing tests fail for reasons unrelated to the deleted branch, which records false "killed" rows. The integration suite could also exceed 210 s, and the worker could miss the deadline. For each deletion, run only the test files that cover it, and drive the tonic and crate tests with `stepWorldTicks`, not real time.

simpler_alternative:
Keep the settled design but make each piece a smaller addition to the existing code:
(1) Implement the hold grace as one read-only `InputGate.worldHoldButtonsAt(frame)`. It returns the last received E/F bits while `frame - heldAtFrame <= WORLD_HOLD_GRACE_FRAMES` (sized as stall plus one resend, about 36 frames) and clears at once when an accepted message drops the bit. Only `stepChannels`, `stepFruits` and `stepClaim` read it; `inputAt`, `lapsedAt` and the simulation's input path stay as they are, so mooring and steering behave exactly as before.
(2) Namespace ledger purchase ids by item (`tonic:<id>`, `rumor:<id>`) in a single helper used by both `chargeRumor` and the tonic purchase, so no client id can make the ledger refuse a delivered rumor.
(3) Make the tonic a request message (with a request id, refused with a reason), not a held button. Store only `tonicUntilTick` on ShipState, set from the ledger's `tonicEffect.endTick`, and scale the per-tick displacement by 110/100 in `sail`. Then prove determinism with the existing input-log replay test extended with the activation event, with no sea prediction.
cheap_experiment: A 15-minute unit probe against the real `InputGate`: feed accepted messages every 6 frames (100 ms), with 0–2 frames of jitter to mimic `sleep(100)` drift. Insert one stall of 18, 24 or 27 frames (300, 400 or 450 ms) at every phase offset from 0 to 5 frames, in both flush mode (held messages delivered when the stall ends) and drop mode. Record the largest received gap in frames and whether it exceeds 30 frames (500 ms). If about half of the 450 ms phases exceed 30 frames, as the arithmetic predicts, the grace constant or the test's stall range has to change before any worker starts. The same probe gives the grace value the operator actually needs: the stall plus one resend period.
